properties.title: DuoPIC: Uncertainty-Aware Voxel-Level Digital Twins of Cerebral Perfusion with Transport PDEs in Acute Stroke

membership.reason: Hybrid physics-informed cerebral perfusion digital twin coupling Windkessel + transport PDEs with a shared mass/MTT-conserving neural closure over dynamic bolus-passage frames.
membership.counting_boundary: Verified L1 hybrid mechanistic-learned organ perfusion model (WT_ORGAN, BP_FORECAST).

properties.backbone: Windkessel flow + advection-dispersion PDE + shared MLP fast/slow pathway closure + tempered posterior

properties.flow: DSC perfusion sequence -> ROI/AIF extraction -> Windkessel + neural transport PDE -> voxel CBF/CBV/MTT maps + 95% uncertainty intervals

properties.purpose: Reference-free, uncertainty-aware cerebral perfusion estimation and ischemic lesion detection in acute stroke.
properties.environment: ISLES'17 MR and 145 ISLES'24 CT perfusion patients

assertions.rationale: Runs on true acquisition time axis from DICOM repetition time Delta (1.4-1.8 s).
Tracer concentration state C(x, t_n) evolved across bolus-passage frames.
Patient/ROI-specific physiological parameters (CBF, CBV, MTT, delay, dispersion) fitted per scan while freezing shared MLP closure.
Temporal evolution of tracer concentration over bolus-passage sequence.
Hybrid Windkessel + transport PDE with population-shared MLP closure.
Indicator-dilution, Windkessel flow, and advection-dispersion PDE conserving tracer mass and MTT.
Couples mechanistic perfusion PDE with shared neural closure.

On held-out patients (5-fold CV), the neural transport PDE predicts hidden/unseen temporal bolus-passage frames better than the compartment baseline in 65% of ROIs, reducing median hidden-frame nMSE from 0.338 to 0.197 with 84.8% hidden-frame 95% interval coverage (Sec. 4 & Table 1, p. 4). Limitation: single-visit bolus-passage dynamics only; paper does not distinguish strictly future tail frames from masked interior frames.
Acute stroke cerebral perfusion quantification and lesion detection.
19% reduction in held-out ROI bolus curve reconstruction error.
Tempered posterior uncertainty lifting 95% MTT interval coverage from 88% to 94%.
Cross-modality validation on ISLES'17 MR (AUC 0.745) and ISLES'24 CT (AUC 0.743).

evidence_fragments.content: We introduce DuoPIC, a digital twin that needs no reference maps, in which a Windkessel flow model drives a tracer transport partial differential equation (PDE). A population-level neural closure divides each region into fast and slow pathways with tracer mass and MTT conserved by construction, and a tempered posterior quantifies the uncertainty of every estimate. Its voxel maps set the state of the art for lesion detection on ISLES’17 MR (AUC 0.745) and ISLES’24 CT (0.743). On held-out patients, the neural PDE reduced the compartment’s reconstruction error by 19% and lifted 95% MTT interval coverage from 88% to 94%.

[paraphrase (visual p.2)] Fig. 1 (p. 2): DSC perfusion MRI input -> signal to concentration, tissue segmentation, GM/WM k-means ROIs, reference-free F/V priors, and automatic AIF + venous correction -> Windkessel flow + delayed/dispersed input driving a 24-finite-volume-cell advection-dispersion PDE split into fast/slow pathways by a shared MLP closure conserving tracer mass and MTT -> voxel-level CBF/CBV/MTT maps and tempered posterior uncertainty (Laplace/MCMC + bootstrap).

The PDE lowered the brain nRMSE, and the neural PDE lowered it further on held-out patients in all five folds (Table 1); on hidden frames, it predicted the curve better than the compartment in 65% of the ROIs (a single tube in 36%).

[paraphrase (visual p.4)] Table 1 (p. 4) held-out diagnostics comparing Compartment / PDE / Neural PDE: Brain nRMSE 0.116 / 0.108 / 0.094; Lesion nRMSE 0.271 / 0.277 / 0.265; MTT 95% coverage 88.1% / - / 93.8%; Hidden 95% coverage 84.0% / - / 84.8%; Hidden nMSE (ROI median) 0.338 / 0.333 / 0.197; AIC below compartment 27% (PDE) / 64% (Neural PDE).

capability_assessments.rationale: Hybrid mechanistic-neural perfusion PDE digital twin with persistent tracer concentration state C(x, t_n), temporal advection-dispersion PDE dynamics, population-shared neural closure plus patient-specific parameter identification, and evaluated hidden-frame bolus-curve prediction on held-out patients (Hidden nMSE 0.197 vs 0.338; L1). Limited to single-visit dynamic bolus passage without longitudinal progression or treatment-intervention conditioning.

readiness_assessments.legacy_highest_label: R2 Multi-dataset retrospective stroke imaging validation

limitations: Fits single-visit dynamic perfusion bolus rather than longitudinal multi-visit progression or treatment interventions.
notes: All 5 physical PDF pages extracted/read; page 2 visually inspected via rendered PNG.

legacy_cells.B: DuoPIC: Uncertainty-Aware Voxel-Level Digital Twins of Cerebral Perfusion with Transport PDEs in Acute Stroke
legacy_cells.C: Tran, Anh Duong, D., Quang-Anh N., Pham, Toan Sy, Hoang, Trang H., Do, Minh N., Mai, Duy Ton, et al.
legacy_cells.S: Estimate voxel-level cerebral blood flow, blood volume, and mean transit time from perfusion time-series data, with uncertainty; evaluate lesion discrimination.
legacy_cells.T: ISLES’17 cohort: 43 subjects with DSC perfusion and final infarct masks; ISLES’24 cohort: 149 subjects with CT perfusion and follow-up MRI masks (145 with infarct outcome in view).
legacy_cells.AI: Dynamic susceptibility contrast (DSC) perfusion concentration-time curves; MR perfusion and CT perfusion images.
legacy_cells.BL: Per-scan repetition time from DICOM metadata: 1.4–1.8 s.
legacy_cells.BN: Windkessel flow and tracer-transport PDE; two-tube neural closure constrained to conserve tracer mass and preserve CBF, CBV, and MTT; physiological parameter priors.
legacy_cells.BS: Fitted/predicted tracer concentration curves and voxel maps of CBF, CBV, and MTT, with posterior standard deviations and 95% intervals.
legacy_cells.BV: Normalized curve reconstruction loss with log-space priors; shared neural closure trained by summed patient losses plus a penalty favoring one pathway rate; posterior likelihood derived from the fit loss.
legacy_cells.DQ: 43 ISLES’17 subjects; 149 ISLES’24 subjects (145 with infarct outcome in view).
legacy_cells.DX: Hidden-frame nMSE: neural PDE 0.197 vs compartment 0.338; brain nRMSE: neural PDE 0.094 vs compartment 0.116 and PDE 0.108.
legacy_cells.EA: The neural PDE preserved physical quantities by construction; normal grey-matter medians were CBF 52 ml/100 g/min, CBV 4.2 ml/100 g, and MTT 4.9 s.
legacy_cells.EG: Fitting approximately 2 × 10^5 voxels per patient took about 100 s on one CPU thread.
legacy_cells.EI: Compared ISLES maps, HemoPIC, oSVD, compartment/PDE variants, ID-CBV, and vendor maps; DuoPIC mean lesion AUC was 0.745 on ISLES’17 and 0.743 on ISLES’24.
legacy_cells.EK: Compared compartment, single-tube PDE, and neural-PDE variants; removing the most uncertain voxels raised MTT lesion AUC from 0.755 to 0.787.
legacy_cells.EL: Semi-synthetic intervals remained too narrow for MTT and relaxation time (τ); neural-PDE 95% coverage was 93.8% for MTT and 78.4% for τ.
legacy_cells.ER: The study used open-access ISLES’17 and ISLES’24 data; their licenses require no ethical approval.
legacy_cells.FL: Patient-specific Windkessel haemodynamics and tracer-transport PDE, coupled to a shared MLP that predicts a conservation-constrained fast/slow pathway split; ROI and voxel fits produce perfusion maps and posterior uncertainty. No planning module is evaluated.
legacy_cells.FM: Introduces a reference-free, uncertainty-aware cerebral perfusion digital twin; a shared physics-preserving neural closure for transit-time heterogeneity; and voxel-level maps evaluated for lesion detection.
legacy_cells.FN: On held-out patients, the neural PDE reduced compartment reconstruction error by 19% and raised 95% MTT interval coverage from 88% to 94%; lesion AUC was 0.745 on ISLES’17 MR and 0.743 on ISLES’24 CT.
legacy_cells.FO: Absolute perfusion values still depend on the automatic arterial input function, and the reference infarct also reflects treatment.
legacy_cells.FQ: The authors identify limitations of HemoPIC: reliance on reference deconvolution maps, inability to represent capillary transit-time heterogeneity under a well-mixed regional assumption, and no uncertainty quantification.
legacy_cells.FR: The paper demonstrates perfusion-curve reconstruction, parameter estimation, uncertainty, and retrospective lesion discrimination—not treatment-conditioned counterfactual reperfusion outcomes, planning/control, prospective clinical benefit, or deployment.
legacy_cells.FS: Reviewer mapping: M3 Belief-state service; M5 Dynamics adapter; M7 Outcome & causal layer
legacy_cells.FT: Reviewer lesson: Expose future-state forecasts through a time-aware dynamics interface and validate error versus horizon; treatment actions need separate evidence before intervention simulation.
